To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effective porosity of the textile implants is a measure of the stability of the textile structure and the effective porosity is reduced by a tensile load in a way that depends on the textile structure.

the structural stability of a textile implant is of high importance for its clinical performance, and that a measurement of the effective pore size is a valuable tool for the assessment of the implant’s suitability for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence.

(a) a high structural stability of a textile implant is required to prevent a collapse of its pores at strain, and (b) the effective porosity of the implant is a measure for its ability to prevent a complete scar entanglement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural stability of textile implants and the effect of a tensile force on the pore geometry.
the development of a method to characterize textile implants in order to predict the structural stability and thus the effective porosity at stress.
the development of new methods for the analysis of textile implants and their application in the field of tissue engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the porosity of textile implants is not a constant value, but is dependent on the strain applied and the structural stability of the textile.
the textile structure should be stable at stress, to prevent pore collapse, and should have sufficiently large pores to prevent a fibrotic entrapment.
the porosity of a textile implant should be measured at strain and that the porosity at strain should not be lower than 10%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measurement of effective porosity can be used to evaluate the structural integrity of a textile implant.
the textile structure of a sling implant has a major influence on its performance in vivo.
high structural stability of textile implants is a prerequisite for a high effective porosity at strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of porosity is a useful method to characterize the textile implant, and that the porosity is a sensitive parameter to indicate the structural stability of the implant.
the measurement of porosity and pore stability can be used as an important quality control for the use of textile implants in tissue engineering.
the structural stability of textile implants can be assessed by a simple method and is of importance for the design and use of implants in the field of regenerative medicine.
